Selling guide

Offer dates vs. pricing to market

Two ways to launch a listing. Which works depends on your home type and how much competition buyers face right now.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
3-minute readFor sellersOntario rules
The short version
  • An offer date lists below value and holds offers to a set day to create competition. It only works when buyers are competing.
  • Pricing to market lists at expected value and takes offers any time. It suits higher inventory.
  • In October 2026, semis sold at 101% of list on average, detached homes at 97%.

01Side by side

Offer date

List below expected value; review all offers at one set time.

Works best when

  • Few similar homes for sale nearby
  • Property types selling over asking
  • Homes that photograph and show well

Watch out for

  • If no one bids, you've anchored buyers low
  • Bully offers need a plan in writing
  • Relisting at a higher price looks like a failed sale

Price to market

List at expected value; review offers as they arrive.

Works best when

  • Plenty of choice for buyers
  • Condos and higher-priced homes
  • Sellers who want a predictable process

Watch out for

  • Overpricing makes the home sit
  • Days on market become a negotiating point
  • Less chance of a bidding war

02What October 2026 says by home type

GTA, all TRREB areas. Higher sold-to-list and fewer days on market mean more buyer competition.

Home typeAvg. sold vs. listAvg. days on marketLeans toward
Semi-detached101%22Offer date can work
Townhouse (freehold)99%28Depends on the street
Detached97%29Price to market
All home types97%31Price to market

Source: TRREB Market Watch, October 2026.

03The rules under TRESA

Written direction

Required

Your agent can hold offers only on your written instructions.

Bully offers

Plan ahead

Your direction must say how pre-emptive offers will be handled. A listing note alone isn't enough.

Changing the date

New direction

You can change it, but everyone who showed interest must be told in writing.

Sharing offer details

Your choice

You can direct your brokerage to share offer details, without names, with competing buyers.

Ali's take

Choose the strategy from the numbers for your home type and street, not from what worked for a neighbour two years ago.
